description: System definition for the completeness vocabulary. Declares why completeness exists and how it is computed.

content.purpose: Tell users at a glance how complete a card is, surface gaps as research prompts, and let the system distinguish stub-quality nodes from verified ones. Completeness is the visible quality dimension of every card.
content.principle: Completeness is per-subtype, not universal. A USGS earthquake legitimately has empty entities[]; a news article does not. The slot spec for each node subtype declares which slots are required, optional, or not applicable. The scorer reads the spec and the envelope, computes filled/total, and returns a tier.

scoring.tiers: Defined in completeness.vocab.tiers — stub <0.4, partial 0.4-0.69, solid 0.7-0.89, verified ≥0.9 with corroboration and no contradictions
scoring.promotion: Nodes auto-promote when they cross thresholds upward (e.g., a partial node receiving more sources becomes solid)
scoring.demotion: Nodes auto-demote when contradictions appear (a verified node with a new contradiction drops to solid)

content.gaps: Unfilled required slots are listed in completeness.gaps with human-readable descriptions. The dashboard surfaces gaps as research prompts; clicking a gap opens an action to fill it (re-run extraction, add a source, etc.).
content.verified_tier_extra_check: The 'verified' tier requires not just score ≥0.9 but ALSO at least one corroboration AND zero open contradictions. Verified nodes are eligible for promotion to epistemic_type='fact' under the assessment rules in nodevocab.
